findings.reason: without naming where the watch path gets a second reading (or extending `published_readings`/the sweep's resolver, and extending the write paths and done-when to prove it through the default resolver), the node lands a two-reading rule that never fires on the caller it targets and the flapping §16 exists to stop persists.
findings.text: the deliverable grounds no source for the second of the two consecutive readings on the watch path: `lift_watch.sweep` reads the group's readings through `_default_readings` → `published_readings`, which returns a single-element list (budget_lift.py:219, `return [payload]`), while the two-reading history builder (`_lift_history`, reckon/budget.py:2640) lives on the pace path that §16 does not name; and `end_cause` is a stateless recompute (budget_lift.py:721) that retains no prior reading, so "a single reading … followed by one that does not" is unobservable as written, and the fix would be inert on the watch stream its own "Why" cites

findings.reason: a test that writes the live lift document or stream reports on the machine rather than the code and can corrupt a peer session's view of what is lifted, and the plan already established the isolation assertion in §13 that §16 omits.
findings.text: §16's done-when has the test call `grant` and `lift_watch.sweep` without stating that the config home and watch stream are redirected to a temporary directory, unlike §13 whose done-when guards exactly this because both writers default to the live `<config-home>/budget-lifts.json` and the real watch stream

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/budget_lift.py`, `reckon/crew/lift_watch.py`, `lift_watch.sweep`, `_reset_observed` and `end_cause` all resolve in the tree (budget_lift.py:721, :802; lift_watch.py:65); the cited `tests/test_a_reset_needs_a_second_reading.py` is the node's own deliverable and need not exist yet.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §16's done-when declares a negative control, but it does not state that the test isolates the config home and stream that `grant` and `lift_watch.sweep` write, where §13's done-when (same plan, `budget_lift.grant` and `lift_watch.sweep` are the same writers) explicitly points the config home at a temporary directory and asserts the real `budget-lifts.json` is byte-identical before and after.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the negative control is logged under the run directory, a durable path a later reader can open; no scratchpad or node-local temporary path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach a symbol or comment; the new test file is named by its mechanism (`test_a_reset_needs_a_second_reading.py`), and `reset`/`end_cause`/`_reset_observed` name mechanisms.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §16's mechanism requires "two consecutive readings with distinct `observed_at` both show" the reset, but the caller the section names, `lift_watch.sweep`, resolves its readings through `_default_readings` → `budget_lift.published_readings`, which returns exactly one reading (budget_lift.py:219), so the two-reading rule can never fire on the watch path where the cited incident occurred.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §16 carries one deliverable: a reset-anchored lift ends only on a confirmed reset and stays ended. The two clauses (confirm on two readings; record the end so a later reading cannot return the lift) are one goal, not two.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `_document` declares `plan-informs background-agent-fitness-and-dispatch-scope` and lists `s16: implementable` in `plan-section-declarations`, matching the section's own `data-status="implementable"`; §16's stated prerequisites (§12, §14, §15) are all `done`, so no dependency it needs is missing.
